title: Quicksilver

description.main: The first volume of Neal Stephenson's Baroque Cycle, a historical novel of natural philosophers, vagabonds, and spies in the late seventeenth century.
description.extended:
Quicksilver is the first volume of Neal Stephenson's Baroque Cycle, a historical novel set mainly between the 1660 Restoration and the 1688 Glorious Revolution.

A frame story opens in Massachusetts in late 1713, when Enoch Root arrives in Boston with a summons for Daniel Waterhouse from Princess Caroline. She wants Daniel to return to England and try to mend the feud between Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz. Flashbacks follow Daniel's life from 1661 to 1673, including his friendship with Newton at Cambridge and his work with Robert Hooke and John Wilkins, while the vagabond Jack Shaftoe and Eliza, a former harem member, cross Europe after the Battle of Vienna. The volume holds three books: Quicksilver, The King of the Vagabonds and Odalisque. William Morrow published it in hardcover in 2003, and it won the 2004 Arthur C. Clarke Award.

The cycle runs to three volumes and eight books and supplies part of the backstory to Cryptonomicon (1999), where Enoch Root also appears.

notes: First edition: William Morrow hardcover, 23 September 2003. Volume One of The Baroque Cycle (Quicksilver, The Confusion, The System of the World). Contains three books: Quicksilver, King of the Vagabonds, Odalisque. Winner of the 2004 Arthur C. Clarke Award.
